title: Lost and Found
logline: At a big city railway station, a counter piled with other people's things waits for owners who may never come, while a clerk decides, item by item, what honesty actually costs.
human_question: What does it cost, in the moment, to hand back something you could easily have kept?

premise.story: A lost-property counter at a major railway or bus station, followed through its daily rhythm of handed-in items, unclaimed shelves and the occasional reunion.
premise.experience: A counter that is half museum, half confessional: bags, phones, umbrellas, a logbook, and the specific moment when someone walks up hoping something is still there.

concept_links.why: The source defines taking what is not given by the plain fact of knowing something belongs to another and deciding to take it anyway [C058-P:L78-L86]. The counter shows the opposite decision, made quietly by strangers, again and again.

what_camera_could_observe: An owner arriving and the moment of return
The clerk's own stories about what does and does not come back
what_must_be_real: A real, working lost-property office and its actual daily traffic. No 'found' items are planted for the camera.

possible_arc.opening: The counter opening for the day, a shelf of unclaimed things.
possible_arc.turn: Someone arrives certain their bag is gone, and finds it.
possible_arc.ending_open: The counter closes with items still unclaimed. Their owners may or may not ever come.

requirements: A railway or bus station with an active, willing lost-property office
Members of the public willing to be filmed retrieving items

suggestions.name: Colombo Fort Railway Station
suggestions.why: A major, well-known station with a long-running lost-property office and high daily traffic.
suggestions.verify: Access and filming permission from railway authorities are unverified.

risks: Filming identifiable members of the public without consent
drop_if: No station will permit filming at the counter
The office's daily traffic is too low to sustain a film

connections.note: Both look at wanting what belongs to someone else, one among strangers at a counter, one among relatives over land.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
